column4: Pixel-art game character sprites in exactly the same style as the reference image: the same pixel size, the same palette and shading, the same rough grain, noise and dither, sallow slightly wrong skin tones and stiff, vacant, unsettling faces. Three figures of the SAME person side by side on one sheet, with wide gaps of background between them so they do not touch, all at exactly the same scale, the feet or knees touching the bottom edge. LEFT: standing facing the viewer, a claw hammer hanging from the right hand. MIDDLE: seen exactly from the side facing right, kneeling on one knee, the hammer raised high above the shoulder about to strike down at a board on the ground that is NOT drawn, the other hand low holding a nail. RIGHT: the same kneeling pose a moment later, the hammer down at ground level, striking. The person: a stocky Czech building labourer of about forty-five in 1998, an unshaven heavy face, a grey knitted cap, faded blue work overalls with a bib over a dirty white vest, a flat carpenter's pencil behind the ear, heavy brown boots, the knees of the overalls muddy. Something about this person is subtly off, like a stranger you would not sit next to. No smile, not cheerful, not clean or cartoonish, the same uncomfortable proportions as the reference. The background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around the figures, no board, no ground, no floor, no ground shadow, no text, no border, no watermark.
